name: Pulp
bio: You don’t need us to tell you who Pulp are, do you? Jarvis Cocker and co have been part of the cultural landscape since His’N’Hers went Top 10 in 1994. What even is British culture without “Common People”? How would we ever have found bittersweet joy in missed romantic chances and the heady pull of nostalgia without “Disco 2000”? Do you even remember the first time?! We’re so excited to welcome Pulp to End of the Road for the first time, hot off the heels of their incredible 2025 album More, 24 years after their last record. Grab your skinniest tie and chunkiest glasses, the 90s are back (again)!

previews.album: Sorted For E's & Wizz / Mis-Shapes EP

name: CMAT
bio: Irish singer-songwriter CMAT had a hell of a 2025: her Mercury-nominated third album Euro-Country was an absolute smash, and her Glastonbury set introduced her dazzling circus of a live show and her irresistibly campy charm to the nation. Of course, we’ve known she was a star on the rise since her 2024 set in the blazing sun on the Woods Stage – no one will forget that Wuthering Heights cover in a hurry, but many have loved her since her first appearance in 2021. She’s back in 2026, bringing her incomparable brand of country-tinged pop to a headline slot. With songs referencing everything from Calpol to the socio-economic plight of her hometown, a CMAT show is a life-affirming, thought-provoking, hands-in-the-air affair.

previews.track: Take A Sexy Picture Of Me
previews.album: Take A Sexy Picture Of Me

name: Mac DeMarco
bio: Everyone’s favourite cheeky Canadian chappy and purveyor of “jizz jazz” is back at End of the Road for 2026. McBriare Samuel Lanyon DeMarco last headlined the Woods Stage in 2017 (he also graced the Garden Stage in 2015), and for 2026 he’s kicked his various trademark vices and is bringing an altogether older, wiser vibe to the festival. On his 2025 album Guitar, he looks back on his salad days from a place of calm, reflecting on a youth thoroughly lived. Forgoing the synths and stripping the music right back to guitar, bass and a smattering of drums that underpin his gentle crooning, we’re looking forward to some old faves drifting out over Larmer Tree Gardens alongside the new.

name: Wild Pink
bio: Since 2015, Wild Pink have been releasing incredible indie-rock songs but on their latest album (2024’s Dulling The Horns), the guitars are more fuzzed out, the songs bigger, and the beats more propulsive than ever before. You could almost imagine Bruce Springsteen coming up with something similar if he’d been born 40 years later and lived in Brooklyn. Crunchy music, mystifying lyrics, and a really good time had by all.

previews.track: Round Of Applause At The End Of The World

name: Westerman
bio: One of the UK’s most vital voices – although these days he’s based in Athens, Greece – Westerman’s graceful songwriting and intricate compositions have won him much critical acclaim. Last year’s A Jackal’s Wedding (folkloric term for a sunshower) is a close, polished record that feints in the direction of pop coloured by Westerman’s trademark folk sensibilities.

previews.album: Cafe Mambo Ibiza: Sunset to After Dark

name: WARBY
bio:
Once upon a time, a man called WARBY spent a lot of time staring at a screen trying to figure out how to get musicians from one place to another. WARBY held a long-term dream that one day he might spend more time at home making music.

One pandemic later…WARBY found he had achieved this ambition & had recorded rough demos of lots of songs. With the encouragement and indulgence of musical friends, these grew into proper recordings and WARBY found that he could perhaps consider himself to be a songwriter & a musician…and not just someone who thought about it.

name: Vicky Farewell
bio: There’s a real air of nostalgia around Vicky Farewell’s glistening, harmony-laden pop. It wouldn’t sound out of place on a Janet Jackson album, or a TLC offcut, with its cascading harmonies and soft but slinky rhythms. Classically trained in piano and fresh from a teenage jazz phase, she’s co-written with Anderson .Paak and toured with Mac DeMarco (whose label she is also on). Her chilled-out, funk-inflected pop is hard to resist.

name: TTSSFU
bio: Meet Tasmin Nicole Stephens, aka TTSSFU, aka “our answer to the question: What if Sky Ferreira were born in Wigan?”. Her dreamy, reverb-heavy pop comes with a healthy sense of humour and some unbelievably strong art-school looks. There’s a darkness to it too, an eerie sense that not everything is quite as it seems. Hotly tipped for big things, catch TTSSFU now so you can say you did later.

name: Tsar B
bio: There are many strings to Justine Bourgeus’ bow – not least as a classical violinist. She’s also an opera and film composer, a producer, a dance maven and a pop polymath as Tsar B, where she mixes baroque stylings with contorted R&B beats to create forward-thinking tunes to get your heart racing and your feet moving.

previews.track: Escalate (live at Les Diners de Gala)
previews.album: Live at Les Diners de Gala

name: Tomo Katsurada
bio: Tomo Katsurada of Japanese psych band Kikagaku Moyo makes solo music that’s tender, dream-like, warm and intimate. Acoustic guitar bobs under floating synths and twinkling piano, and his voice seems to emerge from within. It feels like those moments of unreality between waking and sleeping: playful, spiritual and safe.

name: Tommy Barlow
bio: There hasn’t been a voice as distinctive as Tommy Barlow’s coming out of Cambridgeshire for a while. Mixed with field recordings, guitar, strings, samples and the odd bagpipe, Barlow’s is a delicate sound despite the bold bass vocal, with shades of Mount Kimbie and James Blake alongside more traditional songwriting, with an atmospheric live show to boot.

name: Thredd
bio: “For people who are up for a party, down for a cry” is how London-based art-pop collective Thredd (Imogen and the Knife, Max Winter, Will Lister) describe their debut album, 2025’s It’s Lovely, Come On In. Formed in the basement of dearly departed West London venue Laylow, the trio makes chill, warped electro-pop and vibey, skewed trip-hop – a delicious, refreshing combo they call “cold-pop”.

name: Tex Crick
bio: The crooner vibes are strong with Tex Crick, the Australian singer-songwriter whose music is so laid back it is practically horizontal. Piano-laced lounge-pop with a soft heart, his voice recalls Connan Mockasin and Mac DeMarco, the latter of which signed him to Mac’s Music Label in 2021. With his quiet charm and delightful tunes, his set will be one to savour.

name: Sydney Minsky Sargeant
bio: If his band Working Men’s Club are late nights and neon glistening over dark alleys, Sydney Minsky Sargeant’s solo direction is a gentle breeze ruffling across green fields and sun-dappled naps. Deeply personal and spanning years of his life, these songs are a scrapbook of formative moments laid out in strummed guitars and echoing vocals.

name: Susannah Stark & Band
bio:
Susannah Stark and Band are an experimental ensemble from Glasgow, playing an extended folk session in mystical locations around the Govan stones, river Clyde & underground waters.

Their sound is formed out of sparse sonic gestures and vibrating intensities, weaving among multi-lingual songwriting in both Scottish Gaelic and English, drawing from pop, jazz, experimental, folk & kraut rock influences to create a tactile expression of place, faith and being that can also be experienced as a ritualistic channelling of unseen and unheard forces in everyday life.

Following on from Stark’s debut solo offering of experimental pop, ‘Time Together (Hues and Intensities)’, out on Belgian label Stroom in 2020, is their 2025 album ‘mion-phuingean – Minor Gestures’, a collaborative release with Stroom and Glasgow’s Night School Records.

name: Spanish Horses
bio: Jangly guitar music is back, and Spanish Horses are leading the charge. Formed in Paris, the five-piece have been earning their stripes on the gig circuit in London and mix “various weird, spacey sounds” with driving guitar lines and noisy breakdowns to keep things interesting. This is rock’n’roll for the 2020s, classic but curious.

name: Sophia Stel
bio: Swoony, introspective ballads and gauzy, synth-layered alt-pop are Sophia Stel’s calling card. The Vancouver musician doesn’t use much more than synthesiser, digital drums, and guitar to create her woozy songs, but she swandives through genres and prioritises vulnerability as she does it. Sounds blur together, beats rise and fall, but Stel’s whispery vocal guides you through it all.

name: Snuggle
bio: The cosily named Snuggle sit at “the intersection of bittersweet pop songs and gloomy indie rock”, as The Fader puts it. Their gauzy shoegaze-inspired slacker pop is emotionally charged and full of gentle gloom – never more so than on last year’s debut album Goodbyehouse, full of songs about the major life shifts that unsettle your 20s.

name: SLAG
bio: Brighton newcomers Slag create an irresistible cocktail of mathrock-esque riffs, indie-disco-friendly beats and dreamy pop hooks. Last year’s track “Ripped” caught the attention of buzz-makers, far zippier than its opening lines suggest (“My body is ready to die/It feels like the end of times”) – that, plus their dynamic live show and super cool DIY aesthetic, make for a potent breakout combo.

name: Širom
bio: “Acoustic folk trance drone avant-garde experimental band” is how Širom describe themselves, but if that description has you expecting an absolute racket, think again. Their sound is an intricately woven tapestry of hypnotic, organic textures.The Slovenian band use a host of instruments – banjo, viola, kalimba, bendir, balafon, harps, ukulele, ribab – to create music that takes new and often unsettling, unexpected forms, and sounds like it’s from everywhere and nowhere all at once.

name: Silver Gore
bio: Somewhere between Chairlift and Jockstrap, you’ll find Silver Gore, the delightful pop duo of Ethan P Flynn and Ava Gore. Flynn’s worked with FKA Twigs and Nia Archives while Gore is classically trained; together they’ve created some of the most interesting alt-pop of recent years. On the cusp of bursting out from the underground, you should get in there before they do.

name: Sheherazaad
bio: Sheherazaad defies classification: yes, she’s an American singer-composer, and yes, she’s sort of broadly in the folk-pop wheelhouse, but really she’s all of that and none of it at once. Marrying Western classical and South Asian sounds, her debut EP Qasr is sung in Hindi and Urdu and delves into diasporic displacement and the unbelonging that comes with it. Almost unearthly, Sheherazaad’s music is surreal, radical and completely absorbing.

name: S.G. Goodman
bio: If you’ve been rending your garms to the tones of boygenius and Mitski, then you should get on board the S.G. Goodman train pronto. The Kentucky folk/country singer-songwriter has a voice soaked in sorrow, and her swoony, roots-rock third album finds inspiration in things as small as a suit hanging in a wardrobe and as big as the vast open spaces of childhood.

name: Sex Mask
bio: “Part Taoist riddle, part lone-gun-man manifesto” is how Australian band Sex Mask described their first single in early 2025, and things have only got more winding, intellectual, and satisfyingly constructed since then. That art-school vibe is tempered by a restrained approach to riffs – they kind of sound like The Strokes if The Strokes were about 1000% less self-conscious. But the best way to experience them is live: urgent, propulsive, and so much fun.

previews.album: How To Be Cool At Parties/Circe

name: RÓIS
bio: Northern Irish composer, singer and multi-instrumentalist Róis takes ancient sounds and techniques but makes them sound vital and new. Known for singing in traditional keening caoineadh style, her music aches with grief but just as it threatens to dissolve, ratchets up into frenetic energy and pounding club beats. Totally thrilling to hear and enthralling to watch.

name: RIP Magic
bio: RIP Magic is a London-based band composed of Marco Pini, Felix Bayley-Higgins, Beth Boswell-Knight, and Pedro Takahashi. They formed just over a year ago, after Tyler the Creator singled out their demos while DJing at the Standard. Since then, they’ve had a wild year, dubbed London’s buzziest band by The Guardian and sharing the stage with the likes of Chanel Beads, Lolina, Panda Bear, and Fakemink. Fresh off supporting Fcukers on their EU/UK tour and opening several nights for LCD Soundsystem during their December NYC residency, suffice it to say they’re ones to keep an eye on. While supporting LCD Soundsystem, the band were also quietly selling secret white labels of their next single, “5words,” produced by James Murphy (his first production for another group in over a decade!).

name: Renny Conti
bio: Hailing from the San Francisco Bay Area, there’s a laid-back Californian feel to Renny Conti’s carefully crafted songs. Comparisons to Elliot Smith and Sufjan Stevens are fair, though he’s not exactly like either artist. Folksy and acoustic, he’s inspired by Will Oldham and Harvest-era Neil Young, and each song draws a sweet, often playful, sketch of the small life moments that make up his fears, anxieties, and joys.

name: Prewn
bio: Izzy Hagerup – also known as Prewn – doesn’t shy away from the ugly side of life. Her tormented indie rock is twisted like a house of mirrors and delves into “the sound of your broken, beating, dripping, heaving heart”, as she sings on “Don’t Be Scared”, in a way that is compelling, thrilling and moreish. “Ragged, tormented indie-rock”, as Pitchfork puts it; Prewn is vicious and vital – and really, really great.

name: pollyfromthedirt
bio: If Elliot Smith had a drum machine and an Instagram account – and was from Darlington – he might have sounded a bit like Pollyfromthedirt. The enigmatic masked singer engineers, mixes and masters all his music. The end result is a lo-fi but vivacious dissection of modern England and romances gone wrong.

previews.track: Theres no such thing as england

name: PISS
bio: Brace yourself for some of the most uncompromising and exhilarating punk music you’ve heard in ages. Piss bleed raw emotion and crunching, thundering songs that hit you like a sledgehammer. Hailing from Vancouver, the intensity of the demos you’ll find on Bandcamp is unmatched by their live show: vocalist Taylor Zantingh screams like a deranged preacher amid a whirlwind of sound that’s part exorcism, part horror movie, and all emotional release.

previews.track: What If I Forget The Books

name: Pedro Martins
bio: Pedro Martins is not just a prodigious guitarist with a vibey guitar tone and a penchant for jazz, Brazilian music and pop. He’s also a smooth crooner, his songs shimmying from the jazzier side of things all the way over to synthy 80s pop. Brazil-born and signed to Mac DeMarco’s record label, his intricate guitar lines, innovative compositions, and sundowner feel make for a potent musical combo.

name: ØXN
bio: If you take two members of Lankum, one from Irish experimental rock band Percolator and one established genre-transcending solo artist, you aren’t going to be expecting sunshine, rainbows, and lollipops. OXN deal in the darker side of things: doom folk with supernatural vibrations. They favour murder ballads and nine-minute epics, big, all-encompassing drama always skewing weird whenever possible.

previews.track: The Trees They Do Grow High

name: Ohtis
bio: Illinois country-rockers Ohtis are returning to End of the Road for the first time since 2019. Their dark-folk-americana doesn’t shy away from difficult subjects (depression, addiction, the work you do to recover from both), but it always comes with a glimmer of hope shining through the twang of their guitar lines and Sam Swinson’s morose but endearing vocal. And if you think you don’t know their hit 2021 megahit “Schatze”… you definitely do.

name: Mozart Estate
bio: The singer mononymously known as Lawrence was the subject of Street Level Superstar a few years ago, a biography of a millennium-era almost-was with his bands Felt and Denim (who counted Jarvis Cocker among their fans and peers). In Mozart Estate, Lawrence is embracing the new fans who discovered him via the book, pouring jangly and endearing melodies, and a clear 60s influence into catchy new tunes that may just win him the superstardom he’s been waiting for.

name: Modern Woman
bio: We’ve been Modern Woman fans for so long, it’s hard to believe their debut album is yet to come. But the wait is nearly over – the London art-rock heroes will be releasing Johnny’s Dreamworld in May, stretching their wings with their trademark mix of post-punk, folk and avant-garde instrumentation. With Sophie Harris’s emotive and literary lyricism and the band’s commitment to originality, it’s not to be missed.

name: Misha Panfilov
bio: Misha Panfilov’s approach to jazz is loose and spacey. The Estonian composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist weaves entire universes within the space of one track. Hypnotic but full of life, Panfilov’s swirling compositions blend psychedelic jazz, electronic lounge and ambient music into something you can float off into.

name: Milkweed
bio: Lo-fi trad folk… with hip-hop beats? Milkweed’s music echoes with the ancient sound of wind whistling through the hills, but also gives you a groove you can hook into. Crackling, spooky energy, and a commitment to never showing their faces, they’re a mysterious, dread-inducing duo whose live shows are as intriguing and unsettling as their records.

name: Mia WIlson
bio: There’s a classic Hollywood romance feel to Mia Wilson’s music. Blending piano and guitar with lush orchestral arrangements, her captivating vocals recall Carole King’s Tapestry and other late 60s/early 70s classics. Her self-titled album was released last year and is an inviting collection of songs with a warmth like the first sunny day of spring.

name: Marisa Anderson
bio: “One of the most distinctive guitar players of her generation” is how The New Yorker describes Marisa Anderson, the Portland-based musician and activist. Her technique is silky-smooth, like water running through a babbling brook. Anderson’s compositions are a kaleidoscope of folk musics, touching on blues, jazz, country and gospel, always open-hearted, fluid and masterful.

name: Madra Salach
bio: Madra Salach first caught people’s attention with a live session filmed in a pub on YouTube – their mix of traditional Irish folk and ambient drone is hauntingly beautiful and had everyone who stumbled across the video rapt. The Dublin-based band’s live show is an emotional and timeless experience – one not to be missed.

name: Maddie Ashman
bio: “Uncanny” is a word often used to describe Maddie Ashman’s music: exploring the boundaries of tonality by existing in the spaces between the traditional 12 notes, her microtonal pop often sounds like it’s come from another reality: there’s something a bit unsettling about it. Sometimes wildly beautiful (like last year’s In Autumn My Heart Breaks) and sometimes recalling the atonal pop chaos and hairpin musical turns of Jockstrap, she’s fresh from a support slot with King Gizz and ready to make your jaw drop.

name: M(h)aol
bio: There’s always a sense that anything could happen at a M(h)aol show. The Irish four-piece’s incendiary post-punk is as entertaining as it is invigorating, their conversational lyrics delivered with a dry wit or a furious roar. Nothing is off limits – sexual assault, queer love, societal expectations, misogyny and dead dogs – always delivered with passion and an intersectional approach.

previews.track: No One Ever Talks to Us

name: Little Grandad
bio: The hotly tipped Little Grandad are surfing a wave of buzz all the way to Larmer Tree Gardens with their 90s grunge-meets-Americana. They have a great knack for an earworm and a live show that’s shaded with moments of intensity and trumpet solos. All that plus amazing four-man harmonies and a complete disregard for the conventions of time signatures. Very fun.

previews.album: Babe, We've Run Out Of Time

name: Lily Seabird
bio: Lily Seabird lives in the creative enclave of Burlington, Vermont, in a house share lovingly named Trash Mountain. She named her second album after it, a collection of expressive folk-rock that is both intimate and open, pared back and expansive. She writes about the comings and goings of her life, grief and joy coexisting as two sides of the same coin.

name: Lichen
bio: South London’s Michael Clark has a beguiling voice. As Lichen, he writes haunting tunes about grief and memory that seem to hang in the air even after they’re finished. His debut album, last year’s In My Dreams You Were Golden, is poetic, ghostly, atmospheric, and peppered with glimmering moments of light.

name: Kitchen Lover
bio: Hailing from the ashes of a 1950s punk child, raised in a non-monogamous relationship between The Chats and Dead Kennedys, Kitchen Lover began as a raw-edged two-piece. Before two became three, and three became four—an ever-expanding pack that still grips a visceral core, now laced with a splash of sophistication and undeniable flair. Somewhere between the silver sequin floor and questionable-length shorts, you might call it “strip punk,” though others may say pop disguised as garage rock.

name: Ken Pomeroy
bio: Ken Pomeroy may only be 23, but she’s been playing live since she was 13 – her spellbinding songs bridging the gap between country and folk and spinning stories around you as you listen. Her lyrics often draw on her Native American heritage, delivered in her warm, crystalline twang. As Paste says, “When Pomeroy sings, you pay attention.”

name: keiyaA
bio: With two stunning albums under her belt, keiyaA’s inventive brand of spacey jazz-coloured pop-meets-club-meets-RnB is only getting more thrilling to hear. Last year’s Hooke’s Law is as confronting as it is exposing. It winds its way through the corridors of love and mental health with keiyaA’s smooth vocal guiding the way.

name: Junior Brother
bio: With modern Irish folk that is as challenging as it is unique, as trad as it is modern and as devilishly dark as it is full of hope for a better future, Co. Kerry’s Ronan Kealy is a real one off. As Junior Brother, he blends stark, discordant guitars with accordion, whistles, and other traditional instruments as he sings about politics, division and the climate emergency: no wonder Time Out called his latest album The End “the definitive folk document of 2025.”

name: June McDoom
bio: Alyssa McDoom may have grown up with the offbeat sounds of reggae reverberating around the house, but you wouldn’t know it from her musical alter ego June. Mixing folk, jazz and soul, she’s created an intricate sound, rich in gauzy textures and layered, whispery harmonies. Influences come from all over the place – Joan Baez, The Delfonics, Alton Ellis – but the result sounds cohesive and warm. Music to really sink into.

name: Jordan Patterson
bio: Jordan Patterson could sing the terms and conditions and have you rapt. The LA-raised singer-songwriter-producer triple threat has a voice that has emotion bubbling through it like a hot spring – sometimes it hiccups, other times fizzes mildly, but it’s always raw and unfiltered. Meanwhile her folk and alternative backdrops add a watercolour softness to songs that work through self-discovery, family, and her roots.

name: Jennifer Walton
bio: Jennifer Walton emerged from an array of musical projects (producing, DJing, drumming) with a stunningly lyrical debut solo album last year. Daughters is a stylish and devastating record about the discombobulation of grief, tiptoeing verses give way to bombastic, disorientating choruses – a bit like Björk being dragged through a hedge full of tambourines.

name: Hudson Freeman
bio: If you spend any time on socials, you might recognise Hudson Freeman’s song “If You Know Me”, where it has taken on a life of its own. His songs take on a timeless folk feel, with specks of vintage tape, and slightly soft-focus vocals. Drawing on his unusual childhood (involving evangelical missionaries and a sudden move from Dallas to South Africa), the end result is always reflective, warm, and poignant.

previews.track: The Only Thing I Did Wrong

name: Green Star
bio: From London via Spain and the USA, Green Star mix dreamy shoegaze with the grit of grunge and the earnest heart-on-sleeve sensitivity of 90s emo and come out with something intimate, impassioned and totally brilliant. The trio each take their turn at the mic, making their debut EP – 2025’s Bleeding Swirls – feel like a mixtape in the best way.

name: GNOD
bio: Salford-based psychedelic noiserock overlords GNOD have been keeping us guessing since 2006. Their densely layered music constantly pushes the limits of what can be sonically achieved by a band – not least in the arena of naming albums (see 2017’s Just Say No To The Psycho Right Wing Capitalist Fascist Industrial Death Machine). Incredibly loud, infinitely mesmerising live shows are the cherry on top of the ambiently textured, fuzzed-out, trance-like cake.

previews.album: Gnod Drop Out With White Hills II

name: GHOSTWOMAN
bio: Evan Ushenko and Ille van Dessel are Ghostwoman, a transatlantic twosome making music that lies somewhere between grunge and psychedelia. Their 2025 album Welcome to the Civilized World despairs at the state of things but does so in a thrilling, snarling manner; Ille’s propulsive drumlines underpinning Evan’s hypnotic riffs and impassioned vocals. Everything is rotting, but there’s passion and beauty in it all, too.

name: Garrett T. Capps
bio: We’re going full honky tonk at the hoe down with Garrett T. Capps and his snazzy sunnies. “Cowboy kraut” and “Tex-Mex rock’n’roll” is how he describes it, and he’s a man with a lot of love for San Antonio. Twangy guitars, songs about outer space and inner turmoil and a rootin’ tootin’ good time: what more could you want?

name: GANS
bio: Hooks, riffs and kindness: that’s the GANS formula, and it’s a winning one. The Birmingham two-piece make a racket that’s part hardcore rock and part dancefloor catnip, always accompanied by lyrics that are vulnerable, caring and – as their 2025 debut album is titled – Good For The Soul. Signed to Pete Doherty’s label, a GANS live show is a party that you won’t want to leave.

name: Fine
bio: Mixing strung-out pop melodies with enigmatic electronics and samples and emerging from Copenhagen’s rich alt-pop scene, Fine Glindvad Jensen (pronounced fee-nah)’s solo music unfurls gently as you listen. Her debut, 2024’s Rocky Top Ballads is rich with hazily beautiful music. Songs are whisps sewn together with gossamer threads and Fine’s bewitching, feather-light vocals.

name: Femur
bio: If you like your psych punky and your gigs chaotic, then get to know Femur, the Sheffield four-piece whose unpredictable sound has all the surreal wonkiness of psychedelic noise, all the high energy of punk, and deadpan vocals of grunge. One thing’s for sure: the pit will be feral.

name: Ezra Feinberg
bio: Soft but strong, Ezra Feinberg’s compositions are alive with the sound of nature – they conjure fluttering wings and a breeze ruffling the treetops as he channels his attention into hypnotically beautiful music. Once the leader of Californian psych-rock collective Citay, he now leans into quieter, tender sounds, and twinkling optimism.

name: Ela Minus
bio: Since 2015, Gabriela Jimeno Caldas has been releasing music as Ela Minus, crafting a heady mix of dank club insularity and a wide open, hands-to-the-heavens euphoria. Fresh off the critical success of 2025’s Día and support slots with last year’s headliner Caribou, Ela forgoes computer programmes in favour of manual synths, drum machines and samplers, and the result is dance music with a beating heart.

name: DJ Crenshaw
bio: All vinyl, all gems and the guarantee that all will be rocked: that’s the DJ Crenshaw way. The psychedelic DJ extraordinaire has opened for King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard as well as dazzling audiences from Memphis (Tennessee) to Athens (Greece) with the best of the best dug from his extensive, rare vinyl collection.

name: deBasement
bio: Thundering club energy from party alchemists behind “Front Left Speaker”. Made up of Special Interest’s Alli Logout and DJ and producer Margo XS (who works with Kim Petras and Zara Larsson, among others), you can expect deBasement to come armed with explosive, dancefloor-quaking club bangers and absolutely no holds barred.

name: David Thomas Broughton
bio: An End of The Road favourite returns! You never quite know what you’re going to get when the avant-folk legend David Thomas Broughton takes to the stage – will he serenade a sausage? Will he duet with a rape alarm? He’s a man with a catalogue of delicate songs and a loop pedal he is not afraid to use, so no two shows are ever alike.

name: Daryl Johns
bio: One day you’re a precocious young jazz prodigy and the next you’re making smooth alt-pop instead. That’s just how it goes when you’re LA-based Daryl Johns, now signed to Mac DeMarco’s label and subscribed to the same wavy, chilled out playbook (but with tons more synth and 80s vibes).

name: Colossal Squid
bio: Virtuoso drummer Adam Betts (previously of Three Trapped Tigers, but also Goldie, and Squarepusher) uses drums and electronic pads to create a skittering mass of bangers that deconstruct what a ‘song’ can be and take inspiration from all angles. There’s something new to discover every time you listen – and there’s no better way to do that than as loud and live as possible.

name: Cleo Reed
bio: The phrase ‘genre-bending’ gets thrown around a lot these days but Cleo Reed is really out there doing it. Their 2025 album Cuntry is a record of two halves: the first a mix of strident folk, blues, soul and country, the second sonically disparate, rap-centric and decidedly electronic. This visionary artistry belies the raw, politically engaged lyricism within: totally electrifying.

name: Carson McHone
bio: A Carson McHone song is like a finely woven tapestry: the closer you listen, the more you hear. Tender Americana mixes with richly strummed chamber pop in songs that reach for a greater understanding of what it is to be human. Echoing the raw delivery of Fiona Apple, McHone’s performance on Pentimento proves her voice is as compelling as ever, if perhaps a little more understated.

name: Cardinals
bio: There’s something in the water over in Ireland: band after band are breaking out with fiery, inventive rock music, and Cork-based Cardinals are the latest to join the flock. “What we’re trying to do is just write pop tunes with noise over it,” drummer Darragh Manning explains, of their crunchy, brooding compositions with spritely vocals that sound, whisper it, almost pop-punk. It’s post-pop-punk, if you will, and it’s going to be massive.

name: Brìghde Chaimbeul
bio: It’s bagpipes but not as you know them – Brìghde Chaimbeul (pronounced “Breech-huh Campbell”) has taken the humble pipe and dragged it into the 21st century, mixing traditional Celtic music with experimental sounds and trance-like drone. She plays the Scottish smallpipes that give a mellower sound than the full-on bags, and you might recognise her from her collabs with Caroline Polachek (Blood and Butter), winning the BBC Young Folk Award in 2023 or being bigged up by EOTR fave Gruff Rhys.

Skye Boat Song (Arr. Chaimbeul & Campbell for Violin & Scottish Smallpipe)
Gur Bòidheach Nighean Donn Mo Chridhe

name: Bonnie Dobson & The Hanging Stars
bio: When the renowned Canadian folk singer Bonnie Dobson first jammed with cosmic psych Londoners Hanging Stars, a gently powerful creative force was born. Dobson was at the epicentre of the folk scene in 1960s Greenwich Village: it may be some decades later, but her voice remains as pure and clear as ever. With two collaborative albums under their belt, Bonnie Dobson and the Hanging Stars’ beguiling blend of Americana and psychedelia will have us spellbound.

name: Big Red
bio: Fronted by Joseph Scarisbrick, singer of the mighty The Orchestra (For Now), Big Red started life as a bunch of songs that weren’t quite right for the band. Now it’s sort of the “solo-ish” vehicle for Joseph, a classic set up of guitar, bass and drums delivering songs that rattle with the grit of deconstructed Americana.

name: big long sun
bio: Brighton’s big long sun is the brainchild of Jamie Broughton, a poet, painter, filmmaker and musician whose psychedelic art-pop compositions are brought to cacophonous life by an 8-piece live band. BLS songs wink knowingly at the absurd and constantly zig when you think they’re going to zag, skipping from glorious 60s harmonies to super modern electro noise in the blink of an eye.

name: Bab L’Bluz
bio: Moroccan-French band Bab L’Bluz may make music in a range of styles using traditional instruments, but they are, first and foremost, a rock band. Their music crosses borders, twirling in psychedelic eddies as it trips through Gnawa music, blues, Chaâbi and Afrobeat. Vocalist Yousra Mansour sings in the Moroccan Arabic dialect of Darija and fashioned her own doubled-necked awicha/guitar combo to avoid extra baggage fees.

name: Alice Costelloe
bio: “A document of creative detangling and emotional repair” is how Alice Costelloe describes her first solo album, Move On With The Year. Previously of shoegaze duo Big Deal, her brand of sugar-dusted art-pop belies the vastness of her range – she taught herself flute and piano to open up new melodic worlds after getting sick of the guitar, for example, and you’ll often hear a recorder t

name: Alex Amen
bio: One listen to his music, and you’d be forgiven for thinking Alex Amen was an old man, a septuagenarian reliving his 70s heyday – but his knack for vintage vibes and nostalgic sounds are brand new. Channelling Laurel Canyon’s best and brightest, the Texan nomad’s biggest song to date is California Blues: irresistibly maudlin lyrics with a musical wink to the bright side.

previews.track: Please Don’t Tell Me You Love Me

name: Ak’Chamel, The Giver Of Illness
bio: Weird, wild and wide-ranging, the enigmatic Texan duo that is Ak’chamel, The Giver of Illness pretty much defy description. There’s an earthy feel to their dissonant music; it’s both lo-fi and post-apocalyptic, psychedelic and straightforward. With handmade costumes and self-made instruments, their live show channels the occult, the spiritual and the pleasantly extraordinary. One to be seen to be believed.

previews.track: The Cabinet of the Atomic Priesthood
To Travel The Path Of Every Sickness
The Funeral Of A Woman Whose Soul Is Trapped In The Sun
Amazonian Tribes Mimicking The Sound of Chainsaws With Their Mouths

name: Adult DVD
bio: Adult DVD is not just a spicy Google search, it’s also an infectiously groovy 6-piece with a knack for a juicy hook and foot stomping beat. Call it dance-rock if you like. It’s music that jolts from guitar jangled indie-rock to the euphoria of the club with a sprinkling of acid house in there for good measure, sort of like a modern-day CSS, if CSS were from Leeds instead of Brazil.

name: Working Men’s Club
bio: The thrilling blend of synth-rock, Krautpop, Italian house and stabbing post-punk energy made Working Men’s Club’s self-titled debut one of the most critically lauded albums of that strange year, 2020. Their immersive live show is loud, frenetic and electric, held together by Sydney Minsky-Sargeant’s mischievous yet deadpan vocal. Working Men’s Club will make you dance and make you think.

name: William Tyler
bio: He’s done modern country, he’s done boundary-pushing guitar work, and now William Tyler is taking us through a haunted funfair of strange, claustrophobic music that hunts down and confronts his demons. Previously of Lambchop and Silver Jews, the Nashville-born artist has made plenty of pretty music, but last year’s Time Indefinite is “a vortex of noise”, “haunting, beautiful and unsettlingly close” and one that will stay with you for a long time.

name: YHWH Nailgun
bio: Safe to say, YHWH Nailgun is not going to be for everyone. The New York-based rock band specialises in abrasive and intense shockwaves of sound, pounding rhythms, distorted bass and an absolutely relentless racket. But amid that, you’ll find hypnotic grooves, tension that nearly breaks you and a kind of release you’ll be feeling for hours.

previews.track: Ultra Shade (Beat My Blood Dog Down)

name: The Felice Brothers
bio: Every Felice Brothers song sounds like it could be soundtracking the most poignant indie film you’ve ever seen. The legendary Catskills band somehow tap into the core of things with their deep, cross-genre old-timey Americana. Their live shows are raucous, joyful affairs (but tempered by the sombre and sorrowful, of course): life affirming folk-rock that will send your spirits soaring.

name: PVA
bio: Inventive South London trio PVA make music that straddles the dank pub stage and the glistening, strobe-dappled dance floor. While their debut, Blush, embraced the chaos, the band’s second album, No More Like This (2026), is intimate, sensory dance music that swoons from sultry synths to beats that rush like blood.

name: Model/Actriz
bio: Many attempts have been made to describe Model/Actriz – on their first cacophonous album Dogsbody, they were “post-punk”, “noise-rock”, “techno-metal”, but not really any of those things. On their second, last year’s Pirouette, they lean more towards the listenable (“Inspired by Mariah and Kylie but full of jackhammer rhythms and noise” as The Guardian put it) but no less inventive. And with frontman Cole Haden’s unbelievable stage presence, this is a set not to be missed.

name: mark william lewis
bio: On certain streaming services, you’ll find mark william lewis’s music on a playlist called Sexy Indie, and it’s a perfect descriptor. Sultry guitars and the alluring bass gravel of his voice combine into a sound that practically invites you into bed with absolutely no promise of breakfast the morning after. It makes sense that his moodily charismatic pop netted him the first non-soundtrack deal with A24 Music; it’s as atmospheric and engrossing as a darkened cinema.

name: Just Mustard
bio: Just Mustard’s experimental rock swells with droning guitars and vocals that sound like they’ve been transmitted from another earthly plane. The Irish band’s latest album, We Were Just Here, is a little less abrasive than their previous records, but they’ve lost nothing of their haunting inventiveness or menacing atmospherics in the process.

name: Jeffrey Lewis & The Voltage
bio: That instantly recognisable voice. That scuzzy indie-folk. That unmistakable way with words. Jeffrey Lewis is returning to End of the Road with his delectable blend of acoustic folk, low-fi rock and punk energy that has had a lasting influence on indie and folk since he emerged in 2001. If the end of the world is coming, better believe Jeff’s got something painfully witty and devastatingly incisive to say about it.

previews.track: Except for the Fact That It Isn't

name: james K
bio: Last year was a bit of a break-out year for NYC’s James K, though she’s been releasing moreish, unconventional club music for nearly a decade. Her third album, Friend, taps into the sultry downbeat of triphop – listening to it sort of feels like being enveloped in cotton wool clouds, with passing dashes of breakbeat and pop.

name: Folk Bitch Trio
bio: Melbourne’s Folk Bitch Trio are both less folk and less bitch than their name implies – although they are most definitely a trio. Their sublime harmonies underpin their own brand of indie-pop slash folky-rock, coalescing into something really beautiful on their debut album, 2025’s Now Would Be A Good Time. The trio have been likened to boygenius and Laura Marling, but really they’re something all of their own.

name: caroline
bio: Delicate and surprising, thundering and moving, caroline’s second album, 2025’s caroline 2, is a precious gem of a record, taking in the world with a sense of wide-eyed wonder. The London-based 8-piece make strange, beautiful music (collabs include Caroline Polachek and Jennifer Walton), sort of folk-adjacent but with more than a little mid-west emo, crunchy indie rock and [checks notes] the odd Taio Cruz inspired beat thrown in for good measure.

name: Brakes
bio: The scrappy Brighton indie-rockers have played our first year, our tenth and now they’re joining us for a very special show at our 20th with more fast-paced bangers. The cult faves formed in 2003 and quickly became a mainstay of the UK scene with their spikey riffs and deadpan vocals: and what other band gives you the opportunity to shout “Croque monsieur, croque madame” into the void?

previews.track: All Night Disco Party (Graham Sutton Remix)
previews.album: All Night Disco Party (Graham Sutton Remix)

name: Bassvictim
bio: If you didn’t know that the electroclash revival is in full swing then consider this your wake up call, and leading the charge are London-based duo Bassvictim. Their propulsive mix of distorted bass, hyperpop melodies, extremely 00s aesthetic and intense live show is in the process of bursting out from the underground party scene and bringing all the energy and sweat of the club with it.

name: Anna Von Hausswolff
bio: Gothic legend (and one-time high priestess of satanic harmonies, though don’t take that literally) Anna Von Hausswolff took an unexpected turn towards pop on her sixth album, last year’s Iconoclasts. But if you’re expecting sugary chart-botherers, then think again: amid the glorious, impassioned hooks, you’ll find avant-garde sax improvisations, droning organ and Iggy Pop and Ethel Cain. A “strange, unique, expansive, impassioned and experimental take on pop”, The Guardian says – and unbelievably good, too.

name: Ty Segall
bio: With 17 studio albums under his belt, Ty Segall is not beating the prolific allegations anytime soon. Known and loved for his lo-fi garage rock with psychedelic tendencies, his latest record (2025’s Posessions) leans towards big, feel-good anthems and power-pop numbers. On stage, he’s a firecracker – loud, physical and raw. Earplugs at the ready!

name: Kurt Vile & The Violators
bio: If there was one word to describe Kurt Vile and his music, it’d be: chill. The Philly legend’s laidback psych-inflected indie tunes have been soundtracking our lives since 2008, gently picked guitar endlessly weaving its way around his lo-fi twang. It’s charming, unvarnished and whimsical – just like his hair.

name: Fat Dog
bio: If you haven’t had the sweaty, chaotic pleasure of a Fat Dog liveshow yet, then you haven’t lived. Combining punk, techno, dance and whatever other propulsive, rib-cage-shaking genres take their fancy, the London band make “screaming-into-a-pillow music”, according to frontman Joe Love. Experience the cathartic release and subsequent euphoria of a Fat Dog pit, and you just won’t want to leave.

name: Cowboy Hunters
bio: On their latest single, rowdy Glaswegian punks Cowboy Hunters strongly suggest that since everything is fucked, you might as well Have A Pint. The duo is made up of Megan Pollock and Desmond Johnston, who regularly switch between drums and guitar to make as much noise as possible. They’re pissed off, tanked up and brimming with energy. And they really hate cowboys.

name: Beverly Glenn-Copeland & Elizabeth Copeland
bio: Beverly Glenn-Copeland has spent much of his 60-year career being overlooked. Having started out as a folk singer in 60s Canada, his 1986 album Keyboard Fantasies was way ahead of its time in its use of synthesizers to create warm, minimalist electronica. In the 2010s he finally got his flowers for that record and has since been in high demand, collaborating with Romy, Sam Smith, Arca and Bon Iver while continuing to create and sing his own warm and vital songs as a spry octogenarian.

previews.album: Transmissions: The Music Of Beverly Glenn-Copeland

name: Dave Welder
bio: Not your mate from down the pub, Dave Welder is in fact an ever-changing collection of musicians and artists making esoteric electronic music that takes in dub, ambient, kosmische and drone, and quite often sounds like an interdimensional laser fight being sucked into a black hole. Unbelievably prolific (26 records in a year!), it’s led by filmmaker Ben Wheatley who said of performing live, “I’m really glad I’m doing it, but it’s bizarre.” We have no doubt.

name: Joshua Idehen
bio: Joshua Idehen writes poetry to music. You might have heard Joshua’s viral track ‘Mum Does The Washing’, or caught him featuring on tracks with Sons of Kemet or The Comet Is Coming, but Joshua is really something all of his own. His spoken word creations inspire action and mesh vibrantly with music that inspires movement. His debut album – the catchily named I Know You’re Hurting, Everyone Is Hurting, Everyone is Trying, You Have Got To Try is bursting with jazz-influenced dance tunes that will get your grooving and thinking.

name: Lamisi
bio: Lamisi is one of Ghana’s most strident voices. Her Afro-fusion pop pays tribute to the women and girls of her homeland, who use intricate handclaps and harmonised chants to keep time. African polyrhythms and Lamisi’s warm, soul-inspired voice combine to create something that is both ancient and brand new.

name: Nana Benz Du Togo
bio: Feminist five-piece Nana Benz Du Togo are a force to be reckoned with. Their songs are anchored in the voodoo heritage, and pulse wildly with the value of the earth, wind, fire and water. Freedom is their tenet, and you’ll find it as much in their organic-electronic music and vibrant rhythms as their lyrics, sung in English, French and Mina.

name: Shallowater
bio: Down and dirgy Texan slow-core advocates Shallowater make music that sounds like the moment of half-wakefulness when your body is made of sand and you don’t quite know if you’re asleep or awake. It’s dense but tinged lightly with a touch of Americana, “Raw West Texas dirtgaze”, they call it and righty so – no wonder that Ethel Cain is a fan.

previews.album: God's Gonna Give You a Million Dollars
God's Gonna Give You a Million Dollars

name: Super Furry Animals
bio: Gruff Rhys is a festival regular but it’s been a while since we’ve welcomed the Super Furry Animals to End of the Road. The Welsh icons come with technicolour melodies and a playful mix of indie, pop, psych, and, well, pretty much whatever takes their fancy. Good vibes and endless charm guaranteed.

name: Kiran Leonard
bio: There are at least 19 Kiran Leonard albums out there, and even more under other names: this is a musician who feels the restless need to create coursing through him. His songs are ambitious, dense with words and skittery with unconventional song structures. One second he’ll be strumming an acoustic guitar, the next revelling in an orchestral racket: great joy in experimentation, great charming indie rock and a great sense of humour.

name: Oldboy
bio: You’ll hear them before you see them: Oldboy is the high-octane, crunch-laden project of Max, Ryan and Chris, whose first album, ‘Bloody’ was released in 2022 via Agitated Records to critical acclaim. This was then followed by the ‘Byfleet Dancehall Volume 1’ e.p. in 2023. Prolific they are not. Neighbours as well as friends and collaborators, the Byfleet band was born from a shared love of Fugazi, Pavement and Mudhoney. They finally returned earlier this year with ‘Chicken Fingers’, which has since received notable rotation from John Kennedy and Marc Riley. Produced by Jonah Falco (Fucked Up, High Vis, Home Front), the boys’ new material may have taken longer than the three hours it took to record and mix ‘Bloody’, but it’s guaranteed to be just as explosive. No doubt about it, 2026 is the year of the Oldboy.

name: BCUC
bio: Bantu Continua Uhuru Consciousness, to give them their full name, are a seven-piece band from Soweto, who make infectious pop music that weaves futuristic electronics with afro-pychedelic licks and indigenous music with a rock’n’roll attitude. It’s totally infectious and comes with a live show that is impossible not to enjoy.

name: SILVERWINGKILLER
bio: Half rave, half riot: SILVERWINGKILLER don’t so much play shows as stage ambushes. The Manchester two-piece fuse frenetic breakbeats and snarling analogue arpeggiators with vocals switching between English and Chinese, pulling in world music influences and warping them until they’re barely recognisable. Think sci-fi paranoia meets video game arcana meets pure punk nerve. Barely out of the gate, they’ve already shared stages with Machine Girl, Fat Dog, The Body & Dis Fig and Violent Magic Orchestra – proof that chaos this precise doesn’t stay underground for long.

previews.track: HOLD UP (ALL FIREARMS IN THE UNITED KINGDOM)
previews.album: HOLD UP (ALL FIREARMS IN THE UNITED KINGDOM)

name: Earl Sweatshirt & MIKE
bio: Fans have been gagging for a record from Earl Sweatshirt and Mike since they first toured together in 2019. Their double album Pompeii // Utility finally arrives in April, before they join us at EOTR 2026. An Odd Future alum, Earl has blossomed into one of the most introspective and unconventional rappers working, while Mike has been embraced as a sharp chronicler of life’s downs (and sometimes ups).

previews.track: On God (feat. Earl Sweatshirt & Tony Shhnow)

name: Angine de Poitrine
bio: Do not adjust your dose: the monochrome polka dots and papier mache masks with pendulous noses swinging are real. The duo, known only as Khn (guitars and loop pedal) and Klek (drums), make the most intricate jazzrock prog music you’ve ever heard while leaning into their absurdist visuals. The Québécois duo deal in microtones and math, a bit like Battles if they leaned a little more into funk.

name: Derya Yıldırım & Grup Şimşek
bio: A glorious melting pot of influences make up Derya Yildirim & Grup Şimşek’s sound. From the band’s various backgrounds across Europe and South Africa, to the analogue soul vibes woven through their latest record by way of producer Leon Michels, the result is a smooth and groovy new approach to Anatolian music. Psychedelia, pop and soul all get a look in, as Derya’s limber vocals soar and swoop around it.

name: Factory Floor
bio: You wanna feel kinda weird on the dance floor? Longtime London-based faves Factory Floor have got you. Their spooky, post-apocalyptic post-industrial dance music ricochets with hard beats, minimal synth and androgynous vocals. Once perfectly described by New Order drummer (and FF collaborator) Stephen Morris as “unsettling disco”, gird yourself for an intense but enthralling live experience.

previews.album: Late Night Tales: Barry Can't Swim

name: Rostam
bio: Rostam’s CV is quite something: founding member of Vampire Weekend, writer and producer who’s worked with the likes of Haim, Charli xcx and Frank Ocean, and acclaimed solo artist who deals in songs that feel like a sunrise. His fourth album, American Stories, marries his Iranian heritage with woozy Americana by layering microtonal sax melodies over Western guitar chords.

previews.album: I Had a Dream That You Were Mine

name: Ryan Davis & The Roadhouse Band
bio: Hailing from Louisville, Kentucky, Ryan Davis and his “deep hangdog baritone” (as Stereogum describes it) deal in lyrical Americana that will draw you into a world of dusty streets and cowboy boots. The songs are long and languid, in no hurry as they stretch themselves out into chorus and verse. Formerly of State Champion, Davis’s 2025 album New Threats From The Soul cemented him as one of the warmest, cleverest songwriters working in alt-country today.

name: Way Dynamic
bio: Who else would name an album Massive Shoe but Way Dynamic? The monicker of Melbourne-based songwriter Dylan Young, Way Dynamic’s alt-folk-pop has an endearing silliness to it, tempered by laidback, ambling guitars with a bluesy bent. He writes about the unending struggle that is being alive, but with a lightness that makes it all seem kind of manageable, actually.

name: Another Country $$$$
bio: If you like your experimental dance with a side of live drums and stunning visuals, then you’ll want to be down the front for Another Country $$$$. Coming out of the fervent Manchester DIY scene, the duo’s live sets blend dance music and hyperpop with a variety of niche genre flourishes (vapourwave, anyone?). Euphoria one minute, emo feels the next.

name: Kloyd
bio: If you like the triphoppy chill that Bonobo brings to dance music, you’ll be in your element with Kloyd. The Yorkshire-born, London-based artist mixes dreamy electronica with thumping house beats and abstract vocals to create something that sounds as if it’s being transmitted from a world just slightly off-kilter with our own.

name: Ratboys
bio: The beloved Chicago band blends nostalgic alt-rock with blousy Americana.Their 2026 album Singin’ To An Empty Chair is a warm but curious record – there are as many songs that would be at home on a 90s teen movie soundtrack (one of their influences was Weezer) as there are sittin’-on-the-porch country-tinged epics.

previews.track: At Peace in the Hundred Acre Wood

name: Shaking Hand
bio: Manchester-based three-piece Shaking Hand draw on early post-rock to create songs that evokes the tense guitar lines of Women and Slint, balanced by a vocal that billows across the top. Their hypnotic compositions wind themselves around your brain, with more than a bit of Midwest emo thrown in there for good measure.

name: Yalla Miku
bio: You don’t necessarily expect the most exciting multicultural Krautrock-adjacent psychedelia to come out of Geneva in Switzerland, but Yalla Miku are just that. With members from North and East Africa, the band blends traditional Western song structures with krar riffs, guembri melodies and complimentary electro-pop. Even their name transcends borders: Yalla, the versatile Arabic word used for encouragement, and Miku, the holographic Japanese character from the Vocaloid software.

name: Deary
bio: With hazy guitars, atmospheric production, ghostly vocals and more than a touch of Cocteau Twins about them, Deary are a London trio with a knack for irresistible dreampop. Their woozy songs tend to have a darkness underpinning them – they often write about grief, about nature (their debut album is named Birding) – and have a skewed feel to them that wouldn’t feel out of place in a David Lynch retrospective.

name: Nina Winder-Lind
bio: You might know Nina Winder-Lind from her other life as the cellist in Brighton-based folk-punk band The New Eves, but she’s also a singer-songwriter in her own right. Her first release was the intense but healing The Spirit Is Carnal (2023), a reckoning with her own trauma that mixes poetry with folk, rock, and a dramatic, narrative style.

name: Fatboi Sharif
bio: Deranged, spine-chilling, surreal, intense… these are all words that accurately describe the cursed aura of a Fatboi Sharif track. Listening to his boundary-pushing rap is kind of like being stalked by an entity not of this world: at the very least deeply unsettling (and at the most: actively terrifying). This is hiphop of haunted loops and dense atmospherics, riddled with curses and delivered with dead-eyed intensity. Thrilling in every sense of the word.

name: Kelly Lee Owens (DJ)
bio: Welsh DJ and producer Kelly Lee Owens has put out some of the most gorgeous dance records of the last few years and has one of the most iconic bobs in the business. This summer, she’s joining us for one of her swirling DJ sets where she deftly mixes techno, bass, IDM and the odd pop hook – plus, if you’re lucky, Radiohead’s “How To Disappear Completely”. A dancefloor odyssey that will leave you fully satisfied.

name: Fern Brady
bio: Coming straight outta Bathgate, Fern Brady is Scotland’s second biggest export outside of Iron Bru (don’t google it). She’s an award winning comedian who you may know from her recent specials on BBC and Netflix, or her many TV appearances on the likes of Taskmaster and The Great Celebrity Bake Off. She’s also an award winning, best-selling author. Skills!

name: Desiree Burch
bio: Desiree is a stand up comedian from the US who lives in the UK. A few years ago that would have seemed mad, but kinda makes more sense these days. Over the last 10 years she’s had multiple critically acclaimed stand up shows and has been a regular on TV from Have I Got News To You to Live At The Apollo.

name: Paul Foot
bio: A true comedic pioneer. A master of the surreal, Paul is one of the most influential comedians this country has ever produced. He’s been winning awards for 25 years and we expect he’ll continue to do so.

name: Spencer Jones
bio: A joyous artful absurdist, Spencer’s unique madcap comedy style has earnt him nominations for two BAFTAs and two Edinburgh Comedy Awards. The star of The Mind of Herbert Clunkerdunk and of Mister Winner, you may have also seen Spencer in Ted Lasso, Upstart Crow, and Live at the Apollo.

name: Shappi Khorsandi
bio: A child refugee from Iran turned stand up star and best-selling author. Shappi is known for her fearless and funny takes on identity, family and modern life. A regular on Radio 4, she’s also starred in I’m A Celebrity, as well as all the comedy panel shows.

name: Stewart Lee
bio: Stewart Lee the comedian is a character played by the comedian Stewart Lee. One of them claims to be an out-of-touch, culturally irrelevant, physically enfeebled man pushing 60. The other superciliously accepts it when critics say he’s the world’s greatest living stand-up, as if it’s so obvious that it’s weird to point it out.

name: Laura Smyth
bio: Laura Smyth is an award-winning stand up comedian and writer from East London. She’s a real force of nature, combining her stadium-ready stage presence with her irresistibly hilarious down-to-earth persona. A regular on Radio 4 and TV shows including Have I Got News For You, Live At The Apollo and many more.

name: Andy Field
bio: Andy Field is a stand up who’s lauded by both critics and his fellow comedians. The tallest comedian in whatever town he finds himself in, he’ll challenge anyone to a walking race. He’s won awards and taken psychedelics (although he’s done one more than the other). Kind heart, odd brain.

name: Marty Gleeson
bio: Marty is an Irish comedian making big ol’ waves with her outstandingly original off-beat wonkiness. One of our favourite new comedians, she’s already been a finalist in Channel 4’s Sean Lock Awards and the BBC New Comedy Award AND won LGBTQ+ New Comedian of the Year.

name: Alexandra Haddow
bio: Alex is an award winning comedian and writer. Originally from the East Midlands and now based in East London, she has supported comedy legends Bill Bailey and Frankie Boyle on tour and written for shows including Have I Got News For You and BBC Radio 4’s The News Quiz.

name: Dom McGovern
bio: Dom is a comedian, writer, and prize-winning hog who kicked off his infectious, irreverent standup style in Australia before moving to London. He’s a co-writer on Chicken Shop Dates and a BBC New Comedy Award nominee. He is also the co-host of cult hit comedy night Slay24, and the drag cabaret night OurGayMaria.

name: Molly McGuinness
bio: Molly McGuinness is a Salford-born comedian whose natural warmth conceals razor-sharp working-class observations. She’s a previous BBC New Comedy Awards finalist, has won Manchester Fringe Comedian of the Year and has provided tour support for Joe Lycett.

name: Frankie Monroe
bio:
Edinburgh Comedy Award winner and Yorkshire’s Biggest Bastard Frankie Monroe is up to something… something very cheeky and silly and BIG!

In The Doghouse with Frankie Monroe is a variety show; it’s a game show; it’s a vehicle! There will be special guests, shit prizes, chaotic games – it’s going to be… a total mess!

name: Katie Norris
bio: Katie is a sensational performer who incorporates the odd song (in both meanings of the word) into her hilarious and unpredictable stand-up comedy. She’s adored by critics and fellow comedians and was nominated for best show at Edinburgh Fringe last summer.

previews.album: Mirabai: A Musical Inspired by the Life of a Saint

name: Sunil Patel
bio: Deadpan joke machine Sunil Patel is one of the most gifted comedians in the UK, and it never looks like he’s even trying. As seen on This Time with Alan Partridge, Stath Lets Flats and that Bank advert on TV with McNulty from The Wire.

name: Jack Shep
bio: Jack was beamed into the nation’s living rooms this year as a cast member on SNL UK (Princess Diana anyone?). He’s previously been a finalist of the BBC New Comedy Awards, and you might have seen him in Ch4’s Big Boys or Netflix’s One Day. He once performed improv comedy at Edinburgh Fringe, for which he cannot apologise enough.

name: Geoff Travis & Jeanette Lee
bio:
Geoff Travis

In 1976, Geoff Travis opened the doors to the first Rough Trade shop, based in Ladbroke Grove, London. Having become a nexus for the do-it-yourself ethos that arose out of the punk scene, and inspired by the community spirit that City Lights bookshop in San Francisco nurtured. A few years later, Geoff found himself with a record label after being asked to help out French band Métal Urbain.

With their second single, Augustus Pablo’s “Pablo Meets Mr Bassie”, establishing Rough Trade’s unblinkered approach to music, it soon became one of the first and most influential independent records on earth.

Helping to discover and define alternative music in the UK and beyond, Rough Trade’s initial roster was a who’s who of the creative vanguard, as The Raincoats, The Fall, Aztec Camera, Cabaret Voltaire and more all found a supportive home with Geoff and co. After a pause during the 1990s, Rough Trade returned at the start of the 2000s. A new era in many ways, but also a continuation of the same pioneering spirit, bold artist-first approach and long-term vision. Soon The Strokes, Arcade Fire, The Libertines, Sufjan Stevens, Alabama Shakes and more would call Rough Trade home. With the label celebrating 50 years since first opening its doors, Geoff continues alongside Jeannette Lee to run Rough Trade from its West London base. Still channelling that punky, do-it-yourself attitude that originally kicked things off, with debuts from The Sophs, My New Band Believe and Tyler Ballgame already in 2026 – although he is pleased his decision to start a label has got him out of weekly stocktakes.

Jeannette Lee

Forged in the crucible of London’s late 70s punk scene, first as an instigator and then as an artist, Jeannette Lee’s subsequent career in music and her long association with Rough Trade have been constantly guided by the authenticity and energy of that formative experience.  After working with her great friend Don Letts to document punk through film and photography, she became a member of Public Image Ltd (PiL) alongside John Lydon and Jah Wobble. The band dissolved in the mid-80s and she started a family, but  soon returned to music on the label side, having found a kindred spirit in Geoff Travis. The pair have worked together since to guide Rough Trade and support generations of visionary musicians. Initially working closely with the label’s signings such Robert Wyatt, Mazzy Star and The Sundays, Jeannette played a key role in forging Rough Trade’s enduring identity, before she also began working with artists directly in a management capacity. With The Strokes, Jenny Lewis, Sea Power, Princess Nokia and Super Furry Animals among the artists to join Rough Trade since its return, and – in a pleasingly full circle moment – Pulp currently on the roster, Jeannette and Geoff have ensured it remains one of the most forward-thinking and influential labels around, as it celebrates 50 years since its genesis this year

name: Ian Leslie
bio: Ian Leslie is the author of acclaimed books on human psychology and behaviour, translated into over a dozen languages. He has written for the Financial Times, the Economist, The Atlantic and the New York Times. He will be joining us to discuss John and Paul: A Love Story in Songs, which tells the story of the intense and intimate relationship between Lennon and McCartney. We think we know John & Paul. We really don’t. At the centre of The Beatles was the volatile, madly creative chemistry between John Lennon and Paul McCartney. This is the story of how two young men merged their souls and multiplied their talents to produce one of the greatest bodies of music in history. It is also a love story, full of longing, laughter, pain and joy. John and Paul has been widely praised as a “masterpiece” and “the new gold standard for Beatles books”. It is a number one Sunday Times bestseller.

name: Tom O’Neill
bio: Tom O’Neill is an award-winning investigative journalist and entertainment reporter whose work has appeared in national publications such as Us, Premiere, New York, The Village Voice and Details. He will be joining us to discuss his most recent book, Chaos: Charles Manson, the CIA, and the Secret History of the Sixties. O’Neill’s quest for the truth led him from reclusive celebrities to seasoned spies, from San Francisco’s summer of love to the shadowy sites of the CIA’s mind-control experiments, on a trail rife with shady cover-ups and suspicious coincidences. The product of two decades of reporting, hundreds of new interviews and dozens of never-before-seen documents from the LAPD, the FBI, and the CIA, Chaos mounts an argument that could be, according to Los Angeles Deputy District Attorney Steven Kay, strong enough to overturn the verdicts on the Manson murders. This is a book that overturns our understanding of a pivotal time in American history.

name: Babak Ganjei
bio: Babak Ganjei is an artist, musician and writer. For twelve years, he hosted the show Hot Mess on NTS with his son. He has written and performed in the short films Waiting For Potato and Freelancer (Blink Productions). In 2006, his band supported Silver Jews, and he didn’t pluck up the courage to speak to David Berman but did watch him lift an amp into the van when loading out. He sent his first email from the Central Saint Martins library in 2001 and vowed the internet would never take off, and has been playing catch-up ever since. In 2024, he had his first major solo exhibition at The Bluecoat in Liverpool called Thanks For Having Me. Since then, nobody has asked him to do any shows, and so he has turned his hand to writing. He will be discussing his debut novel On the Bus Without a Phone, recently published by Rough Trade Books to great acclaim.

name: Elizabeth Alker
bio: Elizabeth Alker is a presenter for BBC Radio 3, where she hosts Unclassified and the afternoon show, Classical Live. She joined the BBC as a researcher in 2003 and soon after became a documentary maker, reporter and presenter for BBC Radio 6 Music. Elizabeth has written for the Guardian, Sunday Times and NME Magazine. She will be discussing Everything We Do Is Music a panoramic exploration of how 20th-century classical music, experimental composers, and technological innovations shaped modern pop, rock, and electronic music. The worlds of pop and rock owe a much greater debt to the classical canon than we realise. A direct and fascinating lineage draws from the experimentalism of Pierre Henry to The Beatles’ ‘Tomorrow Never Knows’, from Stockhausen to Donna Summer’s ‘I Feel Love’ and from Bruckner to Sonic Youth via Glenn Branca.  Alker shines a light on the fertile ground that exists between the borders of classical music and pop. She showcases the innovators of the former and their fans and collaborators in the latter, and explores how these artists, together, challenged the notion that such musical worlds are mutually exclusive.

name: Lanre Bakare
bio: Lanre Bakare was born and grew up in Bradford, West Yorkshire. He writes for the Guardian, where his work focuses on the intersection of art, race and culture across multiple disciplines. He was senior correspondent on the award-winning Cotton Capital project, and his debut non-fiction book We Were There was published by The Bodley Head in 2025. It was chosen as a 2025 book of the year  by GQ, Esquire and the Observer. He will be joining us to discuss We Were There: How Black culture, resistance and community shaped modern Britain. From the late 1970s to the early 1990s Britain was in tumult: rocked by Margaret Thatcher’s radical economic policy, the rise of the National Front, and widespread civil unrest. With anti-immigration policies in the political mainstream, Black lives were on the frontline of a racial reckoning. But it was also a time of unrivalled Black cultural creation, organising and resistance. This was the crucible in which modern Britain came into existence.

name: Alice Vincent
bio: Alice Vincent is the author of four books, including Why Women Grow and Rootbound: Rewilding a Life, both longlisted for the Wainwright Prize and named as ‘Books of the Year’ by the Financial Times, Independent, Stylist and others. Alice is a columnist for the Guardian and writes for titles including Vogue, Financial Times and the Sunday Times. She writes Savour, a newsletter dedicated to the delicious things in life, and hosts the Why Women Grow and In Haste podcasts. She lives in South London and will be joining us to discuss Hark: How Women Listen. We’re told women are good at listening, but we rarely examine what they’re listening to, what their worlds sound like, or how it feels to be expected to listen in a world of noise made by men. Like so many of us, Alice Vincent had become overwhelmed by the sensory overload punctuating our every moment. And then, a baby’s heartbeat arrived. A rapid, pulsing whoosh of white noise. An undeniable rhythm. Once again, Alice’s life became cacophonous, both with a new child and with the societal pressures that motherhood holds.

name: Lori Inglis Hall
bio: Lori Inglis Hall was born and raised in Leicestershire, and now lives with her family in East Sussex. She holds an MA in History and previously worked in politics and the arts. She will be joining us to discuss her debut novel The Shock of the Light, published earlier this year to great acclaim. In The Shock of the Light we follow twins Tessa and Theo who had always shared everything – until the summer Tessa spent studying in France. She hasn’t been the same since. But before Theo can find out why, he is recruited by the RAF and disappears into the skies. Determined to carve her own path, Tessa joins the clandestine Special Operations Executive, slipping into the shadows of occupied France. It will be dangerous work, but France is the home of her greatest love – and her darkest secret. Tessa has many reasons for wanting to return. Two years later, only one of them comes home.

name: Nadia Beard
bio: Nadia Beard is a journalist, critic and pianist. Her writing on art, books, culture and politics appear regularly in the Financial Times, New Yorker, National Geographic, Guardian, Economist and Times Literary Supplement, among others. In addition to her writing, she is also the programme director for ZEG Storytelling Festival and managing editor at Coda Story. Nadia was editor-in-chief of The Calvert Journal. Prior to that, she was Moscow correspondent for The Independent. She will be joining us to discuss The Melody of Things: On Returning to Forgotten Joys. How do we lose touch with the things we love? And is it possible to find our way back to them? These pressing questions drive Nadia Beard on a quest to reclaim the dreams of her childhood for her adult self. Many, if not most of us, set aside the pursuits of youth once the reality of working life sets in, leaving the joys and skills of those days far in our slipstream. The Melody of Things depicts what coming back to those early loves entails, as Beard uproots her life to return to study the piano, years after she had stopped playing as a teenager. Beard explores the pleasures, frustrations and revelations of re-dedicating herself to the instrument as an amateur. Her story is an invitation: to seek out the restorative power waiting to be discovered in the pieces of ourselves we have, perhaps unknowingly, lost to time.

name: White Denim
bio: Trying to pin down White Denim is a bit of a fool’s errand. The Austin-formed band have spent nearly two decades blending garage rock, jazz, soul and psychedelia into a sound that rarely stays in one place for long. Early records like Workout Holiday introduced their raw, genre-defying approach, while later releases such as Corsicana Lemonade brought a more polished but still adventurous sound. At the centre of it all is James Petralli, whose distinctive guitar work and vocals anchor the band’s constantly shifting style. Known for their dynamic live shows and fearless musicianship, it all clicks into something genuinely unpredictable on stage.

previews.track: There's A Brain In My Head

name: Perfect Binding
bio: Perfect Binding is the recording project of London-based songwriter and composer Sam Bedford. Worthy of comparisons to the likes of Robert Wyatt, Colleen, Cat Power or Elliott Smith, Bedford’s work lives in the in-between – neither lo-fi nor polished, neither throw-back nor contemporary. With their debut EP released in August 2025, Perfect Binding offers a compelling introduction to a songwriter focused on tone, tension, and emotional undercurrent.

name: Bug Teeth
bio: Bug Teeth began as the electronic bedroom project of PJ Johnson before evolving into a full band, with live performances that drift between fragile stillness and bursts of distortion. Pulling from dream pop, ambient electronics and fractured breakbeats, Bug Teeth craft songs that feel hazy, immersive and hard to pin down. Their debut album, Micrographia, expands that world further, balancing beauty with abrasion and grief. With a growing cult following, Bug Teeth continue to shapeshift and spirit listeners somewhere between waking and dreaming.

name: multiscreen
bio: Blending 80’s-inspired dance-pop with digital-age emo, multiscreen confronts what it is to be a young person on the internet in a manner that is critical – but not relentlessly doomy. 2025 singles “That’s life” (with strings written and performed by Saya Barbaglia of Mary In The Junkyard) and “It’s hip to be dumb” both explore this through textured ambient sounds, distinctly playful synths, and detached pop sensibilities.

name: Al Cologne
bio: London-based artist Al Cologne’s sound is charged with an electric, queer tenderness, gently fizzing with emotion that has condensed over years of diaristic, kitchen-sink songwriting. Yearning, intimacy, and sexual discovery are bottled in songs shaped by mood rather than fixed arrangement. Their debut EP Milk Teeth, released in March 2026, drifts in the orbit of Angel Olsen, Sharon Van Etten, Big Thief, and Faye Webster.

name: Geese
bio: What’s there to be said about Geese that you don’t already know?! Did you know they played The Big Top at End of The Road in 2023? They’ve been pretty busy since. Frontman Cameron Winter released his breakthrough solo record Heavy Metal in 2024, and the full band followed suit with their equally beloved breakthrough Getting Killed in 2025. With Getting Killed, Geese balances a disarming new tenderness with an intensified anger, seemingly trading their love of classic rock for a disdain for music itself. An addictive listen, shambolic in structure but passionately performed, Getting Killed is informed by an exacting vision. We’re so excited to have them back to execute that vision writ large on our main stage.

name: The Space Lady
bio: From the pavements of Boston in the 70s and San Francisco in the 80s, The Space Lady’s story is quite the odyssey. After her accordion was stolen, she invested in a Casio keyboard, a phase shifter and a headset mic, and something magical was born. The Space Lady takes pop songs and beams them back to us from somewhere far beyond, shimmering with peace, harmony, and pure wonder.

previews.track: I Had Too Much to Dream Last Night

name: Rose of Nevada: Live Score by the Cornish Sound Unit
bio: BAFTA-winning filmmaker Mark Jenkin and musician Dion Star make music that feels like it was pulled from the earth. Working with tape loops, analogue synthesis and improvised sound design, their live performances are raw, evolving, events – never quite the same twice. Originally commissioned by the BFI to score Jenkin’s folk-horror film Enys Men, they return in 2026 with the live score for his new film Rose of Nevada, starring George MacKay and Callum Turner.

name: Brother Wallace
bio: If you’re in the market for a shot of pure joy, Brother Wallace has what you need. A junior school music teacher turned show-stopping soulman, his debut record Electric Love is bursting with timeless songs that sound like they wouldn’t be out of place on a Nancy Meyer OST (complimentary). Electrifying vocals and unbelievably good vibes, the kind of music that puts a grin on your face no matter your mood.

name: 1000 Rabbits
bio: Stitched together with playful synths, violin, guitar and drums, 1000 Rabbits build emotionally raw songs that feel immediate and immersive. The Brixton Windmill regulars deliver high-voltage sets packed with off-kilter rhythms and ever-evolving sounds, capturing the spirit of free-form jazz through an abrasive modern lens.

name: The Cindys
bio: Born from Jack Ogborne (aka Bingo Fury), with help from Naima Bock, Finlay Burrows and members of Belishas, The Cindys chase surrealist imagery and irresistible hooks at breakneck speed. Their self-titled debut album,, tracked between Falmouth, Rockfield and Bristol’s Louisiana cellar, arrived via Breakfast Records and Ruination, earning tours with Shame and Getdown Services.

previews.track: I'm Pursuing A Career Outside Of Conveyancing

name: Ninush
bio: Nina Lim has spent years lending her bow to London’s alt-scene royalty and soaking up their sounds along the way. As Ninush, she steps out solo, spinning emotionally raw songs that flicker between tenderness and technicolour, pop hooks wrapped in kaleidoscopic strangeness.

name: Bo Ningen
bio: Since coalescing in London, Bo Ningen have blurred the line between music and art, collaborating with Alexander McQueen, Damo Suzuki, and Jehnny Beth alike. Their ferocious live shows have earned a fearsome reputation worldwide, pairing chaotic anarchy with genuine artistic invention at every turn.

name: Drook
bio: Drook keep transforming, from guitar-driven indie pop to dream pop to club-ready electronics, landing on 2024’s manic, energetic The Pure Joy of Jumping. Formed at VCU over shared breakfasts and anime marathons, theirs is a sound that refuses to sit still.

name: Irma Vep
bio: Irma Vep is a 1996 French comedy-drama film written and directed by Olivier Assayas. Hong Kong actress Maggie Cheung plays a fictionalised version of herself, as disasters result when an unstable French film director attempts to remake Louis Feuillade's classic silent film serial Les Vampires (1915–16); Irma Vep is an anagram for the word "vampire". Taking place largely through the eyes of a foreigner (Cheung), it is also a meditation on the state of the French film industry.

name: Spend It All
bio: Les Blank was an American documentary filmmaker best known for his portraits of American traditional musicians.
